task.name: turing/common-ground-ballot
task.description: Private membership ballot workspace with fixed eligibility, two voting methods, revision-safe lifecycle controls, anonymous results, and durable audit history.

metadata.provenance: Adapted from the repository's original Common Ground request and the real user task-intake conversation for this workspace; expanded into the standardized full-stack contract on 2026-09-04
metadata.arena_slice_note: The 0.273 figure is the measured backend/db/auth single slice. It is not an intersection rate for the full stack or this domain.
metadata.invariant_family: eligibility snapshots, one-person-one-ballot enforcement, anonymous selections, idempotent retries, revision-safe lifecycle changes, exact tallies, and auditable turnout
metadata.difficulty_explanation: A compact six-workspace product combines two ballot methods, fixed eligibility, anonymous choice storage, identified turnout, exact result math, durable sessions, role boundaries, optimistic revisions, and idempotent write receipts.
metadata.solution_explanation: The reference solution uses one Express process, normalized SQLite tables, hashed bearer sessions, transactional lifecycle and vote writes, replay receipts, revision guards, and a responsive vanilla browser client.
metadata.verification_explanation: Render and Constraints are small hard gates. Functional browser criteria follow seeded decisions through draft, eligibility, private voting, closure and publication, with narrow same-origin request replay for server enforcement, revision, and idempotency checks.

before.name: distinct_sessions_and_global_revocation
before.description: Open two independent signed-in browser contexts for Ruth. Sign out normally in the first context: its protected requests must now be refused while the second still loads Ruth's workspace after refresh. Sign Ruth in again in the first context, then use End all sessions there. Both contexts must now lose protected access, including on refresh, while a fresh sign-in still succeeds. A local-only logout, ordinary logout revoking the other session, or either session surviving End all sessions fails.

after.name: distinct_sessions_and_global_revocation
after.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. Open two independent signed-in browser contexts for Ruth.
2. Sign out normally in the first context: its protected requests must now be refused while the second still loads Ruth's workspace after refresh.
3. Sign Ruth in again in the first context, then use End all sessions there.
4. Both contexts must now lose protected access, including on refresh, while a fresh sign-in still succeeds.
5. A local-only logout, ordinary logout revoking the other session, or either session surviving End all sessions fails.
Before each sign-out, retain the actual session credential used by a successful protected read. After ordinary sign-out, replay that read with the ended credential; after End all sessions, replay it with each ended credential. Every replay must return non-2xx. Use the browser request context with captured authentication headers for HttpOnly cookies, or a same-origin request with the actual bearer header; do not mutate browser cookies/storage or print credential values. An unauthenticated request after merely clearing a local cookie is not proof of server revocation.

before.name: durable_reauthentication_and_seed_safety
before.description: After the completed workflow, record the full visible ballot collection, statuses, revisions, turnout, published tallies, roster, and audit count. Run the trusted command python3 /tests/app-lifecycle.py restart, which restarts only the app without resetting its database. Refresh existing staff and Member sessions and require them to remain authenticated with the same accepted data. Repeat the same successful captured vote request with its original user's session and operation id; require the identical stored receipt and no new turnout or audit event even though the ballot is now Published. Restart once more, then refresh, sign out and sign in again. Require exactly the same accepted records and values, no duplicate seeds or votes, and no return of rejected writes. Do not inspect or edit SQLite to satisfy this criterion.

after.name: durable_reauthentication_and_seed_safety
after.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.

4. Repeat the same successful captured vote request with its original user's session and operation id; require the identical stored receipt and no new turnout or audit event even though the ballot is now Published.
5. Restart once more, then refresh, sign out and sign in again.
6. Require exactly the same accepted records and values, no duplicate seeds or votes, and no return of rejected writes.
7. Do not inspect or edit SQLite to satisfy this criterion.

before.name: accessible_keyboard_forms
before.description: Use keyboard navigation through sign-in and a representative ballot or voting form. Require visible focus, logical focus order, associated labels or accessible names, keyboard-operable choices and buttons, a closeable dialog without a focus trap failure, and navigation/main landmarks with meaningful headings.

after.name: accessible_keyboard_forms

before.name: ballot_result_visual_hierarchy
before.description:
Across a staff ballot list, detailed turnout, and a published approval result, require a coherent hierarchy, readable labels and values, scannable status treatment, useful empty/restricted states, and a visual result treatment that still exposes exact counts and approval percentages as text rather than raw JSON or an unlabeled graphic. Use the approval result published in the functional workflow, or publish the seeded closed approval ballot as Ruth if necessary; do not assume all seed ballots are still in their initial states.
Rate 1 for missing, unreadable, raw-data-only, or heavily overlapping views; 3 for readable values with inconsistent grouping or minor crowding; and 5 when all listed views have clear grouping, readable status/count/percentage text, and no overlap. Use 2 or 4 for intermediate quality. Assess visual presentation here, not correctness of the already-graded tally calculations.

after.name: visual_color_and_contrast
after.description:
Assess colour and contrast on the rendered signed-in surfaces in both light
and dark themes (use the visible theme control and return between them).
5: cohesive palette; text and background contrast stays legible; status and
accent colours are distinguishable; both themes preserve readability.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: noticeable low-contrast text or clashing accents in one theme.
2: substantial legibility problems or an inconsistent palette.
1: colours are broadly default or harsh, or one theme is difficult to read.
0: no readable colour treatment renders on the reviewed surface.

after.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
after.description:
Assess visual hierarchy and scannability on the rendered signed-in workspace
at desktop width.
5: clear visual order - brand and navigation, workspace title, section
groupings, and primary figures and actions each have distinct prominence, so
the current workspace, key numbers and main actions can be found by scanning.
4: hierarchy is mostly clear with minor ambiguity.
3: several sections compete, or important content is visually buried.
2: navigation, headings and content are hard to tell apart.
1: no usable visual hierarchy is present.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders on the reviewed surface.

after.name: visual_overall_craft
after.description:
Assess overall visual craft across several rendered signed-in surfaces
(Ballots, Turnout, Results and Members), including secondary,
empty or loading states you encounter.
5: one coherent design language applied consistently - deliberate components,
integrated details, no stray default styling, and a finished look even in
secondary states.
4: one or two minor polish imperfections.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent component treatment across workspaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or inconsistent.
1: visual craft is effectively absent.
0: no crafted interface renders on the reviewed surfaces.

after.name: visual_responsive_consistency
after.description:
Assess visual consistency across desktop and a roughly 390 by 844 mobile
viewport on the rendered signed-in workspace (Ballots and the
Turnout workspace).
5: the same design language holds at both sizes - text, spacing, cards, tables
and controls scale or reflow deliberately without squashing, stretching,
overflow beyond intentional scroll areas, or visual breakage, and the
light/dark change preserves that consistency.
4: one or two minor responsive visual defects.
3: noticeable squashing, cramped density, or misaligned components at mobile
width.
2: several components break or overflow badly on mobile.
1: mobile rendering is visually inconsistent or mostly broken.
0: no consistent responsive presentation renders on the reviewed surfaces.

after.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
after.description:
Assess spacing and layout on the rendered signed-in workspace at desktop width
(Ballots, Turnout, and one ballot detail or form surface).
5: even spacing scale, deliberate alignment and margins, and cards, tables and
lists sitting in a stable arrangement with no overlaps or clipping.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several elements look crowded, drifting, or unevenly padded.
2: frequent collisions, clipping, or inconsistent gutters.
1: layout is broadly unbalanced or broken.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders on the reviewed surface.

after.name: visual_typography
after.description:
Assess typography on the rendered signed-in workspace at http://localhost:3000
at desktop width (Ballots plus Turnout and Results).
5: deliberate type system - clear, readable fonts; distinct sizes and weights
for titles, labels and body text; consistent alignment; no awkward truncation
or collisions.
4: readable with one or two minor size or alignment defects.
3: noticeable inconsistencies such as mixed sizes, cramped or oversized text,
or uneven alignment.
2: several labels are hard to read or inconsistently styled.
1: typography is broadly default, illegible, or misaligned.
0: no coherent typographic rendering exists on the reviewed surface.
